linh: Heads-up — found inflated pass@k numbers on the quantized model bring-up. A lot of top-k candidates are duplicates or near-duplicates, which is artificially boosting pass@k. Opening thread to capture repro and a deterministic fix.

omar: Can you paste a tiny example of the candidates you saw? Is it exact string duplicates or whitespace/punctuation/tokenization variants?

linh: Example from one eval case (k=5):
[
  "def add(a, b): return a + b",
  "def add(a,b):return a+b",
  "def add(a, b): return a + b",
  "def add(a, b):\n    return a + b",
  "def add(a,b):return a+b"
]
This ends up counting as multiple unique answers in naive pass@k impl. Some are exact, some differ only by spacing/newline.

maya: Yep — classic duplicate inflation. We should run a normalization step before uniqueness: unicode normalize, collapse whitespace, normalize common punctuation, lowercase where appropriate for the task (or not, if case matters). Then dedupe. Also important: deterministic tie-breaker so pass@k isn't flaky.

sam: Also noticing CI flakes on this test — sometimes sampling returns slightly different ordering so which candidate wins the dedupe can change. CI currently doesn't pin RNG in the smoke eval. Propose we pin seeds for CI runs and still keep real randomness in nightly/regression runs.

rachel: One more wrinkle: the quantized model sometimes changes tokenization boundaries which creates near-duplicates that are semantically identical but token-different. Normalization helps, but for code tasks we might also run a lightweight parser/formatter (e.g., black for py) for normalization when safe.

ci-bot: CI job #4521 failed: eval-harness-smoke (pass@k) — flake. Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/4521 (truncated).

omar: Draft dedupe heuristics I use (keeps highest-score candidate for each normalized form, deterministic tie-breaker):
```python
import unicodedata
from typing import List, Tuple

def normalize_text(s: str) -> str:
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)
    s = s.replace('\r\n', '\n')
    s = ' '.join(s.split())  # collapse whitespace
    return s.strip()

# candidates: list of (text, score) sorted by score desc
def dedupe_candidates(candidates: List[Tuple[str, float]]):
    seen = {}  # normalized -> (text, score)
    for text, score in candidates:
        key = normalize_text(text)
        if key not in seen or score > seen[key][1]:
            seen[key] = (text, score)
    # deterministic ordering: sort by score desc then text asc as tiebreaker
    kept = sorted(seen.values(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    return kept

def compute_pass_at_k(candidates: List[Tuple[str, float]], references: List[str], k: int) -> float:
    kept = dedupe_candidates(candidates)[:k]
    kept_texts = [normalize_text(t) for t, _ in kept]
    ref_norm = {normalize_text(r) for r in references}
    return float(any(t in ref_norm for t in kept_texts))
```

maya: That looks good. Two notes: 1) keep normalization configurable by task (don't force lowercase on case-sensitive tasks), 2) add a small deterministic salt to tie-breaker when text equal but scores exactly equal (rare, but avoids non-determinism).

linh: I'll open a PR to add normalize_text + dedupe pipeline to eval-runner and add unit tests that assert deterministic ordering (seeded RNG + expected kept set). Will also add an integration test that runs with the quantized model snapshot we used for the regression.

sam: I can add a CI env var (EVAL_DETERMINISTIC=1) that the job will set for smoke runs so we pin RNG and pass that into the runner. For nightly jobs we leave it unset. :thumbsup:

rachel: For the reporting dashboard, we should add a note/tooltip explaining "pass@k after dedup" vs raw pass@k so analysts understand differences during bring-ups. Also add a diff column comparing deduped vs raw so we can spot tasks where dedupe materially changes metrics.

linh: Great. I'll reference this thread in the PR description and tag @sam for the CI change. Thanks all :eyes:
